content:
Facts: Son challenged deceased mother's 1999 typed holographic will claiming apocryphal signatures based on handwriting analysis; will published 2000 with heirs' express Art. 590 acceptance despite invalidity-awareness; defendant contested limitation-period objecting acceptance validated null will; expert confirmed signatures apocryphal using imitative-transparency process; accountant-witness testified mother signed in presence but other witness denied recalling mother's office-presence; plaintiff sought intestate-succession declaration, asset-return, estate-division.
Legal Framework: Articles 590, 602, 606 Italian Civil Code (null-will validation through confirmation/execution; holographic formalities; nullity); Arts. 1113, 784 CPC (registered-creditor joinder requirements); case law on Art. 590 applicability limits (Cass. 13487/2005, 40138/2021, 10065/2020).
Interpretive Issues: Whether Art. 590 validation operates when holographic will lacks/contains forged signature; distinction between will-nullity and non-existence; evidentiary value of will-drafting circumstances regarding authentication; registered-creditor joinder necessity for division-proceedings validity; effect of untruthful witness-testimony on authenticity-assessment; criminal-proceedings retraction-request relevance.
Principles Applied: Art. 590 permits null-will confirmation/execution by heirs knowing nullity-cause after testator-death (express-confirmation) or voluntarily-executing (tacit-confirmation). Basis: preservation-principle more-justified for mortis-causa acts because author unable renewing transaction eliminating invalidity-cause; intention allowing relatives respecting deceased-memory executing last-will even formally/substantially non-complying with legal-provisions. Issue: whether exceptional null-act remedy operates when signature lacking/forged. Doctrine/case-law argue will improperly-formed or forged-signature not merely null but non-existent; signature-function not purely-formal but solemn-confirmation of written-provisions/completeness plus testator-origin. Alternative doctrine permits holographic-will-without-signature or non-attributable-signature confirmation given Art. 606 wording "null if lacks handwriting/signature"; incomplete deed-deceased connection cannot be disregarded. Cassation case-law unanimously adheres first-interpretation; Art. 590 inapplicable when holographic-will signature absent/false. Signature-requirement purpose (Art. 602 distinct from provision-handwriting): satisfying absolute-certainty need regarding provisions' testator-referability (holograph-ensured), unequivocal-authorship/responsibility of testator who after drafting (even different-times) disposed estate without second-thoughts. Inauthentic-signature precludes Art. 590 application; presupposes objective-existence of testamentary-provision although-null nevertheless deceased-will result. Negative-origin-assessment claim amounts authenticity-challenge; formal forgery-complaint unnecessary (Cass. 18363/2018). Court-appointed expert: signatures X1/X2 affixed will-margin/bottom apocryphal, not belonging to deceased-hand. Detailed comparative-analyses confirmed apocrypha; graphic-trace contradictions/rhythmic-inconsistencies consisting slowness/awkwardness/uncertainty alternating sudden-briskness/speed plus qualitative/substantial discrepancies from different-incompatible graphomotor-nature. Vague external-similarities between letters/graphic-dimensions/hold/arrangement attributable to imitative transparency-process. Superimposability/equivalence shapes signatures X1/X2 with analyzed-handwritten signature regarding medium-long letters-dimensions, stability/arrangement versus baseline, combined rhythmic-inconsistency/graphic-incoherence contribute determining apocryphal-nature. Highly-unlikely same-writer same-day could affix two examined-signatures showing hesitations/uncertainties/ink-smudges versus handwritten-signature lacking such elements. Expert-comparison particularly-significant: signatures compared handwritten-signature affixed notarial-rectification deed same-day as contested-will drafting; contemporaneity gives particular graphological-assessment significance. Unequivocal expert-findings fully-acceptable regarding logical-presentation/argument-consistency, graphometric-elements clarity. Anomalous-circumstance: deceased visited notary for rectification-deed, accountant drafted invalid-will (handwritten-text lacking) same-day; unclear why deceased after notary-visit where public-will drawable preferred dictating testament to accountant. Accountant-testimony (mother signed presence 3.9.1999) contradicted witness denying recalling mother-presence accountant-office given time-elapsed. No mother's office-presence evidence beyond untruthful accountant-testimony. Criminal-proceedings retraction-request unnecessary given consistent-facts/convincing-uncontested expert-conclusions rendering referral-back superfluous. Will non-originating from deceased ascertained; legitimate-succession opened with assets devolving equally to heirs per Art. 566. Estate-asset return follows succession-opening declaration; legitimate-heir cannot request inherited-asset return before division-operations. Division-proceedings continues without registered-creditor adversarial-integration need (Cass. 6228/2023): creditor/assignee joinder not division-validity condition but obligation if co-owners want decision binding them; joinder-failure doesn't invalidate judgment regarding co-owners but entails Art. 1113 consequences (creditors/registered-purchasers may challenge-division if violation-caused damage, disallow division-effectiveness tam-quam-non-esset). Investigating-judge correctly initiated proceedings absent creditor-identification documentation; disputed-extension unnecessary for decision-validity.
